items.prompt: A configuration flag read at runtime selects either a capped or identity implementation for a DynamicAdjust reference. Why is replacing that reference with StaticAdjust<Cap10> alone not behaviorally equivalent?

options.text: That specialization fixes Cap10 and removes runtime policy choice.
options.why: A single static specialization cannot change its template argument from a runtime flag. Preserve runtime selection with an appropriate wrapper/branch/interface.

options.text: A virtual interface requires every implementation to be heap allocated.
options.why: The lesson uses automatic DynamicCap storage; runtime dispatch and allocation strategy are separate.

options.text: CRTP cannot share the twice implementation between policies.
options.why: That sharing is precisely what the displayed CRTP base demonstrates; selection capability is the gap.

options.text: All uses of runtime configuration make noexcept invalid.
options.why: Reading a selected nonthrowing implementation through an established interface is not inherently throwing; noexcept and selection are separate contracts.

items.explanation: A single static specialization cannot change its template argument from a runtime flag. Preserve runtime selection with an appropriate wrapper/branch/interface.
